toegepas.rede_vinder: An impersonal passive in Afrikaans normally takes 'daar'; without it the clause reads clipped.
toegepas.fout: The impersonal passive 'wanneer geplant moes word' lacks the 'daar' Afrikaans normally uses, so the clause reads clipped.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Adding 'daar' is the natural Afrikaans impersonal passive and leaves who plants, and when, unchanged.

na_skrywer.voor: Wanneer mense saam aan iets werk om mekaar te help.
na_skrywer.na: Om saam met ander aan iets te werk en mekaar so te help.
na_skrywer.rede_vinder: Defining a noun with a 'wanneer' clause copies the English 'is when' pattern; an infinitive definition is the natural Afrikaans form and keeps the meaning.
na_skrywer.fout: The definition uses the English 'is when' pattern ('Wanneer mense ...') to define a noun.
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: The fault is real, but this is a glossary definition and the rewording goes beyond a spelling or grammar fix, so the writer must change it for every lesson at once.
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: kon so 'n nuweling kalwers vir 'n jaar of twee leen
laat_vaar_vorige.na: kon vir 'n jaar of twee kalwers aan so 'n nuweling leen
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Leen' can mean lend or borrow; 'aan' makes it unambiguous that the community member lends to the newcomer.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The original double-object 'iemand iemand iets leen' already means lend, not borrow (community member to newcomer); the reordering places 'n jaar of twee' directly before 'kalwers', which a Grade 5 reader can misread as 'one or two calves'.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: Matches the past tense of the main clause and of the next sentence ('gehad het').
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: Afrikaans has no sequence-of-tenses rule, so 'het gesorg dat dit goed gaan' is natural and correct; changing the tense is a lateral move.
